requirements.quote: An Initial packet uses long headers with a type value of 0x00.  It
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the long-header form and a packet type value of 0x00.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding an Initial packet with a short header or a packet type value other than 0x00.
requirements.why_checkable: The header form and type bits can be inspected directly in an encoded Initial packet.

requirements.quote: Header Form (1) = 1,
requirements.condition: When encoding or validating the Header Form field of an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the 1-bit Header Form field with value 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using any Header Form value other than 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and fixed value are directly observable in the wire encoding.

requirements.quote: Fixed Bit (1) = 1,
requirements.condition: When encoding or validating the Fixed Bit of an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the 1-bit Fixed Bit with value 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a Fixed Bit value other than 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and fixed value are directly observable in the wire encoding.

requirements.quote: Long Packet Type (2) = 0,
requirements.condition: When encoding or validating the Long Packet Type field of an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the 2-bit Long Packet Type field with value 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a Long Packet Type value other than 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The two-bit field and its fixed value can be checked in the packet header.

requirements.quote: Reserved Bits (2),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the Reserved Bits field with a width of 2 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a Reserved Bits field width other than 2 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width follows directly from the packet layout and can be checked in serialized packets.

requirements.quote: Packet Number Length (2),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the Packet Number Length field with a width of 2 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a Packet Number Length field width other than 2 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width can be verified against the serialized header layout.

requirements.quote: Version (32),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the Version field with a width of 32 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a Version field width other than 32 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded field has a fixed, directly measurable width.

requirements.quote: Destination Connection ID Length (8),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the Destination Connection ID Length field with a width of 8 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a Destination Connection ID Length field width other than 8 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded field has a fixed, directly measurable width.

requirements.quote: Destination Connection ID (0..160),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Destination Connection ID of an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Destination Connection ID with a length from 0 through 160 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding a Destination Connection ID longer than 160 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The field length can be measured in a serialized packet and checked against the stated bounds.

requirements.quote: Source Connection ID Length (8),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the Source Connection ID Length field with a width of 8 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a Source Connection ID Length field width other than 8 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded field has a fixed, directly measurable width.

requirements.quote: Source Connection ID (0..160),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Source Connection ID of an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Source Connection ID with a length from 0 through 160 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding a Source Connection ID longer than 160 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The field length can be measured in a serialized packet and checked against the stated bounds.

requirements.quote: Token Length (i),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent Token Length as a variable-length integer field.
requirements.why_checkable: The field's use of the variable-length integer encoding can be checked in serialized packets.

requirements.quote: Length (i),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent Length as a variable-length integer field.
requirements.why_checkable: The field's use of the variable-length integer encoding can be checked in serialized packets.

requirements.quote: Packet Number (8..32),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Packet Number field with a width from 8 through 32 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding the Packet Number field with a width below 8 bits or above 32 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded packet-number width can be measured and checked against the stated bounds.

requirements.quote: Packet Payload (8..),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode a Packet Payload of at least 8 bits.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding an Initial packet payload shorter than 8 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload length can be measured directly in the serialized packet.

requirements.quote:
The Initial packet contains a long header as well as the Length and
   Packet Number fields; see Section 17.2.  The first byte contains the
   Reserved and Packet Number Length bits; see also Section 17.2.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a long header, Length field, and Packet Number field, with the Reserved and Packet Number Length bits in the first byte.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omitting these fields or locating the Reserved or Packet Number Length bits outside the first byte.
requirements.why_checkable: Field presence and placement can be verified from the serialized packet layout.

requirements.quote:
Between the Source Connection ID and Length fields, there are two
   additional fields specific to the Initial packet.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the two Initial-specific fields, Token Length and Token, between Source Connection ID and Length.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omitting these fields or placing them outside the interval between Source Connection ID and Length.
requirements.why_checkable: The required field identities derive from the adjacent packet layout and their order is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote:
Token Length:  A variable-length integer specifying the length of the
      Token field, in bytes.  This value is 0 if no token is present.
requirements.condition: When an Initial packet contains no token.
requirements.required_behavior: Set Token Length to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a nonzero Token Length when no token is present.
requirements.why_checkable: Token presence and the decoded Token Length value can be compared directly.

requirements.quote:
Initial packets sent by the server MUST set the Token Length field
      to 0; clients that receive an Initial packet with a non-zero Token
      Length field MUST either discard the packet or generate a
      connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: When a server sends an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the Token Length field to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A server sending an Initial packet with a nonzero Token Length field.
requirements.why_checkable: A server-generated Initial packet's Token Length can be decoded and compared with zero.

requirements.quote:
Initial packets sent by the server MUST set the Token Length field
      to 0; clients that receive an Initial packet with a non-zero Token
      Length field MUST either discard the packet or generate a
      connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a server Initial packet whose Token Length field is nonzero.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Continuing to process the packet normally without either permitted response.
requirements.error_behavior: Either discard the packet or generate a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: A focused receive test can inject the invalid field value and observe discard or the specified connection error.

requirements.quote:
Token:  The value of the token that was previously provided in a
      Retry packet or NEW_TOKEN frame; see Section 8.1.
requirements.condition: When an Initial packet carries a Token field.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the token value previously provided in a Retry packet or NEW_TOKEN frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a Token value that was not the value previously provided through either source.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded token can be compared byte-for-byte with the token previously issued to the endpoint.

requirements.quote:
In order to prevent tampering by version-unaware middleboxes, Initial
   packets are protected with connection- and version-specific keys
   (Initial keys) as described in [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When sending an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Protect the packet using connection- and version-specific Initial keys.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending an Initial packet without this protection or protecting it with keys not specific to its connection and version.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can derive the expected Initial keys for the connection and version and verify packet protection and decryption behavior.

requirements.quote:
The client and server use the Initial packet type for any packet that
   contains an initial cryptographic handshake message.
requirements.condition: When a client or server creates a packet containing an initial cryptographic handshake message.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Initial packet type.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Placing an initial cryptographic handshake message in another packet type.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet type can be correlated with the presence and phase of the cryptographic handshake message.

requirements.quote:
This includes
   all cases where a new packet containing the initial cryptographic
   message needs to be created, such as the packets sent after receiving
   a Retry packet; see Section 17.2.5.
requirements.condition: When a new packet containing the initial cryptographic message is created after receiving a Retry packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Initial packet type for the newly created packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using another packet type for the recreated initial cryptographic message.
requirements.why_checkable: A Retry-driven test can observe the type of the subsequently created packet containing the message.

requirements.quote:
A server sends its first Initial packet in response to a client
   Initial.
requirements.condition: When a server sends its first Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Send it in response to a client Initial.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending the server's first Initial packet before receiving a client Initial.
requirements.why_checkable: A packet trace can verify the causal ordering of the client and server Initial packets.

requirements.quote:
The payload of an Initial packet includes a CRYPTO frame (or frames)
   containing a cryptographic handshake message, ACK frames, or both.
requirements.condition: When constructing the payload of an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include CRYPTO frame(s) containing a cryptographic handshake message, ACK frame(s), or both.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Constructing the payload without either a qualifying CRYPTO frame or an ACK frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded frame sequence can be inspected for at least one of the specified frame categories.

requirements.quote:
PING, PADDING, and CONNECTION_CLOSE frames of type 0x1c are also
   permitted.
requirements.condition: When selecting additional frame types for an Initial packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit PING, PADDING, and CONNECTION_CLOSE frames whose type is 0x1c.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treating these listed frames as prohibited solely because they occur in an Initial packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame-type validation behavior can be tested with Initial packets containing each listed frame.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that receives an Initial packet containing
   other frames can either discard the packet as spurious or treat it as
   a connection error.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives an Initial packet containing a frame other than CRYPTO, ACK, PING, PADDING, or CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1c.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accepting and processing the packet normally.
requirements.error_behavior: Either discard the packet as spurious or treat it as a connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: A receiver can be given each disallowed frame type and its discard or error outcome can be observed.

requirements.quote:
The first packet sent by a client always includes a CRYPTO frame that
   contains the start or all of the first cryptographic handshake
   message.
requirements.condition: When a client sends its first packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a CRYPTO frame containing the start or all of the first cryptographic handshake message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending the first client packet without such a CRYPTO frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The first client packet and its decoded CRYPTO-frame content can be inspected in a packet trace.

requirements.quote:
The first CRYPTO frame sent always begins at an offset of
   0; see Section 7.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends its first CRYPTO frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the frame's starting offset to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending the first CRYPTO frame with a nonzero starting offset.
requirements.why_checkable: The first transmitted CRYPTO frame's offset is directly available from the decoded frame.

requirements.quote:
Note that if the server sends a TLS HelloRetryRequest (see
   Section 4.7 of [QUIC-TLS]), the client will send another series of
   Initial packets.
requirements.condition: When the server sends a TLS HelloRetryRequest.
requirements.required_behavior: The client sends another series of Initial packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client continuing the response exclusively with non-Initial packet types.
requirements.why_checkable: A handshake trace can inject a HelloRetryRequest and observe the client's subsequent packet types.

requirements.quote:
These Initial packets will continue the
   cryptographic handshake and will contain CRYPTO frames starting at an
   offset matching the size of the CRYPTO frames sent in the first
   flight of Initial packets.
requirements.condition: When the client sends the new Initial-packet series after a TLS HelloRetryRequest.
requirements.required_behavior: Continue the cryptographic handshake and start its CRYPTO frames at an offset equal to the size of the CRYPTO frames sent in the first flight of Initial packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Starting the new series' CRYPTO data at an offset different from the size of the first flight's CRYPTO frames.
requirements.why_checkable: The prior flight's CRYPTO-data size can be calculated and compared with the starting offset in the post-HelloRetryRequest Initial series.
